dcb1fb8a500b2bc4515e729a3696cd477b6e0c8d.summary: This article reports on AlphV's own statement about its ransomware attack on MGM Resorts International in September 2023. AlphV says it kept administrator access to MGM's identity and cloud systems, launched ransomware against more than 100 ESXi hypervisors on September 11, and still had access to some infrastructure. It denies claiming the attack before it did, and says news outlets wrongly reported that it had. The article notes that a LinkedIn social-engineering claim was never confirmed. All of AlphV's claims are its own and unverified.

dc2c89b00c82c6d21a1a745693b916b4a2a7c8ef.summary: A news report says Universal Health Services (UHS), a healthcare provider with facilities in the US and UK, shut down systems across its US hospitals in a suspected ransomware attack in late September 2020. Employees reported files renamed with a .ryk extension and a ransom note resembling Ryuk's. The report says the attack likely began with phishing, and that Emotet and TrickBot had been detected affecting UHS earlier in 2020. UHS confirmed an IT security incident and said no patient or employee data appeared to have been accessed. Four deaths were reported but not independently corroborated.

dca972746c383a4c3b9c0852963aa4f9e01ab265.summary: CrowdStrike's blog on the 2021 Kaseya attack, in which REvil ransomware operators used zero-day vulnerabilities to push a malicious update through Kaseya VSA. CrowdStrike links REvil to the PINCHY SPIDER group and says its Falcon platform would have blocked the attack. Reported figures include fewer than 60 Kaseya customers and 1,500 downstream companies, a $70 million ransom demand that may have been lowered to $50 million, and an operator claim of more than 1 million infected systems.

dc03a067735360acad3b1053e3fb9302e6609192.summary: The report describes RTM, a banking trojan written in Delphi and first seen in telemetry in late 2015. It targets accounting staff and remote banking users, mainly in Russia and neighboring countries, and is spread through drive-by downloads and spam. It logs keystrokes, takes screenshots, watches banking windows and smart card readers, and looks for accounting export files. Its command and control uses Namecoin-based names. Shared certificates and a Buhtrap downloader link RTM to Buhtrap, but the report believes the two groups are different.

hedges: The report believes RTM and Buhtrap are different groups, though they share a similar modus operandi and some certificates and infrastructure.
The report is not sure of the purpose of the botnet-prefix value and says it may only record a version.
The report hypothesises that the VNC module lets criminals connect remotely and then move laterally, which is not shown directly.
The report believes the 1c_2_kl module is still in development because it contains debug messages.
The report gives the company names on the code-signing certificates as 'allegedly' called those names.
The report says the RC4 modification is possibly meant to slow down security researchers' analysis.
The report notes that a low detection count suggests targeting of high-value victims, while mass spreading means detections outside Russia are not surprising.
